login.title: Sign in
login.hint: Your desk name and password. The session lives in an httpOnly cookie and can be ended — from here or from any other browser you left it in.
login.tokenFallback: Sign in with an identity token instead
login.tokenFallbackHint: Each identity's token is written to .data/secrets/<slug>.token. If this machine predates passwords, sign in with the token and set a password from the Models tab.
login.badCredentials: That name and password do not match.
errors.wordedForTheMachine: It did not go through, and no reason came back that a person could read.
setup.title: Claim this machine
setup.lead: This machine has no owner yet. Create yours — it becomes the first account, with its own agent and workspace. You can add an AI provider later; the OS runs without one.
setup.localOnlyNote: Setup only accepts requests from the machine itself (localhost or your SSH tunnel), and only until the first owner is created.
setup.errorNotLocal: Setup can only run on the machine itself. Open this panel on the box, or over your SSH tunnel.
setup.errorAlreadyClaimed: This machine already has an owner. Sign in with a token instead.
desks.heading: Your desks
desks.hint: You, and the agents you own. Pick one to see its home, sessions, and activity.
teammate.hint: Create another user on this machine — you'll get a token to hand them.
teammate.created: Created {slug}. Share this token with them:
approvals.heading: Approvals — awaiting your consent
approvals.hint: Actions any of your agents parked for a decision. Each binds to the exact request it previews.
desk.homeVolumeHint: This desk keeps its own space, {slug}. It outlives every screen you open — nothing here is lost when one closes.
desk.title: Your screens
desk.lead: The Linux screens on this machine — the desktop you sit at, and the terminal Cielo works in. Open one, take a seat at Cielo's, or close one you have finished with.
desk.kindDesktopHint: Windows, a browser and the tools this desk comes with. It opens in a tab of its own.
desk.kindTerminalHint: Text only. This is the screen Cielo works on, and you can type on it too.
desk.opened: Opening a screen for {who}. It takes a few seconds to come up.
desk.setupNotReady: Your desk is set up as {label}, and that setup has not been built on this machine yet — no screen can open until it is. Build it under Desk setups below.
desk.loading: Reading the screens on this machine…
desk.loadFailed: Could not read the screens on this machine: {reason}
desk.empty: No screens are open. Open one above; it keeps running, and everything on it stays put until you close it.
desk.seatHint: Watching leaves Cielo working; taking over puts you at the keys. Either one is written down in Activity, in your name and Cielo's.
desk.blockedPopup: If nothing opened, your browser held the tab back. Open it yourself:
desk.closeHint: Closing a screen throws away whatever is still running on it, so the machine stops and asks you first.
desk.screenLead: What is on this terminal right now, read again every few seconds.
desk.screenNone: No terminal is running. Open one above — choose Cielo and A terminal — and its screen appears here.
desk.screenPick: Pick a terminal above and its screen appears here.
desk.screenNotRunning: This screen is not running, so there is nothing on it to show.
desk.typePlaceholder: type a line, then press Enter
desk.typeHint: What you send lands on the same screen Cielo is working on, exactly as if you had typed it there. Every line is written down in Activity.
desk.typeFailed: That line did not go through: {reason}
desk.setupsLead: What comes installed inside a screen. A setup has to be built on this machine before a screen can open on it, and the build downloads gigabytes and takes minutes.
desk.setupsFailed: Could not read the setups on this machine: {reason}
desk.setupsEmpty: This machine reported no setups. Nothing here can add one — they arrive with the installation.
desk.setupBuildStarted: Building {label}. It runs in the background and takes minutes; you can carry on.
desk.setupJob: {label} is building. It keeps going if you close this window.
files.sharedHint: You and your agents share this. Drop inputs here; the agent leaves results here. (~/shared)
files.binaryNotice: A binary file ({size} B) — download it to open in the right application.
files.errorNoHome: There is no space for '{owner}' yet. Open a screen for this desk and one is made.
files.errorNoShared: No shared workspace yet — open a session (its ~/shared provisions it).
files.leadYours: Your documents, and everything Cielo has made for you.
files.leadOther: What {owner} is working with. You can read it here and save a copy.
files.leadShared: The workspace you and Cielo share — what you hand over, and what it hands back.
files.truncatedNote: Only the first part is shown. Save the file to read all of it.
files.kindSpecial: Not a file that can be opened or saved.
files.emptyYours: Nothing here yet. What you save, and what Cielo makes for you, lands here.
files.emptyOther: Nothing here yet. What {owner} makes lands here.
files.emptyShared: Nothing here yet. Leave a file here for Cielo to work on — it leaves what it makes here too.
files.emptyRecordings: No films yet. When Cielo's screen is filmed, the file is saved here.
files.notYetYours: You have no files yet. This fills in the first time you or Cielo works on this machine.
files.notYetOther: {owner} has nothing here yet. This fills in the first time it works on this machine.
files.notYetShared: There is no shared space yet. It is made the first time you and Cielo work together on this machine.
files.notYetRetry: Something is running now — give it a moment, then reload.
files.notAllowed: You are not allowed to read {owner}'s files.
files.listFailedUnknown: Could not open this folder, and the machine did not say why. Reload to try again.
files.readFailedUnknown: Could not open {name}, and the machine did not say why.
files.recordingsNote: Films of Cielo's screen. They stay on this machine and are not sent anywhere. Play one here, or save it.
files.recordingsRowNote: Films of Cielo's screen, kept on this machine.
files.filmLoading: Fetching the film — a long recording takes a moment.
files.filmFailed: This browser could not play {name}. Save it and open it in a video player.
files.filmFetchFailed: Could not fetch {name} to play it.
sessions.heading: Sessions
sessions.hint: A console or desktop over this desk's home. Create is allowed; destroy asks for your approval.
sessions.unavailable: This machine cannot open screens right now — the part that runs them is not answering.
chat.heading: Chat
chat.hint: The full chat runs in CieloOS Chat. Every message puts Cielo to work at its own terminal — it uses its tools and runs this machine — under the same checks as everything else here.
chat.firstAgentCaveat: Note: chat always talks to your first agent, not the desk selected here — per-agent routing needs the per-user credentials tracked in issue #9.
chat.unconfigured: No chat UI is configured on this machine. CieloOS serves an OpenAI-compatible API for one at /v1/agent; point a client at it and set Chat__Url to that client's address to link it here.
console.heading: Console — give the agent a task
console.hint: Cielo drives its own terminal toward your goal — every keystroke is checked and written down. Watch it below.
console.goalPlaceholder: e.g. search the web for the top 10 posts about El Salvador and save them as an Excel file
activity.heading: Activity — {desk}
activity.empty: No activity recorded for this desk yet.
activity.title: Activity
activity.lead: A plain record of what Cielo did, and what you answered. Every answer is kept with the reason that was on screen when you gave it — so you can check later whether you were told the truth.
activity.refreshedNone: Nothing new since you last looked.
activity.emptyBody: This fills itself in: every page Cielo opens, every key it sends, every sign-in, and every answer you give is written here as it happens.
activity.emptyAnsweredTitle: You have not answered anything yet
activity.emptyAnsweredBody: When Cielo stops and asks your permission, your answer is kept here together with the reason you were shown.
activity.failedBody: The runtime would not hand over the record of what Cielo did. It said: {message}
activity.failedUnreachable: The runtime did not answer. It may be starting up, or stopped.
activity.sessionEnded: Sign in again to read the record of what Cielo did.
activity.status.allowedNotDone: You said yes — it did not happen
activity.refusedLine: Cielo asked to do this and the machine said no. Nothing happened.
activity.allowedNotDoneLine: You allowed it, but it did not take effect.
activity.reasonShowing: The reason you are being shown
activity.actors.unrecorded: The record does not name who did this
activity.why.browser.navigate: Opening a page is also how information leaves this machine, and the address it opens is not always one you chose.
activity.why.desktop.type: Anything on the screen Cielo is reading can steer these keystrokes — into a command, or a secret, you never asked for — and they land as if you had typed them yourself.
activity.why.desktop.key: A key Cielo sends lands as if you had pressed it yourself, and the screen it is reading is what decides which key that is.
activity.why.session.destroy: Closing a desk ends whatever was running on it, and anything not saved into your files goes with it.
activity.why.spreadsheet.clear: Clearing cells takes out what was in them, and the sheet has no way back to the numbers that were there.
activity.why.fallback: Cielo stopped and asked because this is the kind of action that cannot be taken back.
activity.action.browser.click: Clicked something on a web page
activity.action.browser.back: Went back to the previous page
activity.action.console.type: Typed a command into the terminal
activity.action.desktop.key: Pressed a key on the screen
activity.action.sessionInput.grant: Let Cielo use the keyboard and mouse
activity.action.sessionInput.revoke: Took the keyboard and mouse back
activity.action.sessionInput.grantVision: Allowed screenshots to be sent to an AI service
activity.action.sessionInput.revokeVisio: Stopped screenshots being sent to an AI service
activity.action.spreadsheet.setCell: Changed a cell in the spreadsheet
activity.action.spreadsheet.sum: Added up cells in the spreadsheet
activity.action.desk.imageBuild: Prepared a new kind of desk
activity.action.shared.download: Downloaded a file from the shared folder
activity.action.runtime.seed: Set this machine up for the first time
security.heading: Sign-in and keys
security.hint: A password proves who you are; a session carries that and can be ended; an API key lets a program act without holding your own credential. Identity tokens still work for agents and the CLI — they never expire, which is why they are not a login.
security.currentPasswordPlaceholder: leave empty if you have none yet
security.passwordNote: Setting your first password must be done on the machine itself. Changing it ends every other session.
security.passwordSet: Password set. Every other session has been signed out.
security.keySecretNotice: Copy it now — it is shown once and only its hash is stored:
usage.heading: Model spend — {month}
usage.hint: Tokens are what a provider bills for, so they are what is counted. On-box models are recorded too, but a ceiling never stops them: they cost machine time, not money.
usage.limitNote: 0 removes the ceiling. A run that hits it stops with an explanation rather than a provider error.
providers.heading: Model providers
providers.hint: The brains your agents use. The OS runs with none; add one and it's usable immediately — no restart. A default is what an agent uses unless it has its own choice.
providers.empty: No providers yet — add one on the right to give your agents a brain.
addProvider.heading: Add a provider
addProvider.errorRequiredFields: Name, base URL, model, and at least one capability are required.
addProvider.providerAdded: Added {name}. Your agent can use it now.
examples.heading: Examples
examples.hint: Each of these runs real commands through the same checks as everything else on this machine. Nothing here is a special demo path — if an example works, the machine works.
examples.notInstalled: This installation does not carry the examples folder.
examples.errorNeedsDesktop: This example runs on a desktop session, and there is no running desktop to use. Open one from Desks first.
examples.title: Try an example
examples.loading: Looking for the examples on this machine…
examples.notInstalledFix: They ship inside the desktop image. Install or update this machine from a bundle that carries them, and they appear here.
examples.errorList: The examples on this machine could not be listed: {detail}
examples.errorLostRun: The run stopped reporting where it had got to, so the position below may be out of date: {detail}
examples.noDesktop: Some examples run on a desktop of their own, and none is running. Start one in the Desk app and it will show up here.
examples.cardNeedsDesktop: Waits for a desktop — none is running.
examples.waitingNote: Nothing happens until you answer. If you set the request aside, it is still here.
examples.progressLabel: How far this run has got
examples.oneAtATime: One at a time — the rest wait until this run ends.
examples.notifyStarted: “{title}” is running. Every step shows up here as it happens.
settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: What Cielo thinks with, what it may spend, who may sign in — and in which language all of it happens.
settings.providers.title: AI provider
settings.providers.lead: The service Cielo thinks with. Add one and it works straight away — nothing to restart. When there is more than one, the default is the one Cielo reaches for.
settings.providers.failed: Could not read the connected providers: {reason}
settings.providers.emptyBody: Cielo needs an AI service to understand what you ask and work out what to do. Connect one and the rest of this computer comes alive — chat, tasks, examples. Your key is kept on this machine and is never shown again.
settings.providers.defaultFailed: Could not change which one Cielo uses by default: {reason}
settings.language.title: Language
settings.language.lead: The language of this panel, and the language Cielo answers you in.
settings.spend.title: Spending
settings.spend.lead: A cloud provider bills for tokens, so tokens are what is counted. A model running on this computer is counted too, but a ceiling never stops it: it costs machine time, not money.
settings.spend.failed: Could not read this month's spending: {reason}
settings.spend.empty: Nothing counted yet this month. Figures appear here the first time Cielo uses a provider.
settings.password.title: Password
settings.password.lead: How you prove it is you.
settings.password.tooShort: A password needs at least {count} characters.
settings.signOut.title: Sign out everywhere
settings.signOut.lead: Ends every session, in every browser and on every machine — including this one. Nothing else is touched.
settings.signOut.done: Every session has been ended. Sign in again to carry on.
settings.keys.title: Keys for programs
settings.keys.lead: A key lets a program act as you without holding your password. Name each one, so you know what you are revoking later.
settings.keys.empty: No keys yet. Create one when a program needs to reach this computer as you.
settings.keys.secretTitle: This is the only time you will see the key for {name}
settings.keys.secretBody: Copy it now. This computer keeps only a fingerprint of it, so it can never be shown again — if you lose it, revoke it and make another.
settings.keys.copyFailed: Could not copy it — select the key and copy it yourself.
settings.people.title: Teammates
settings.people.lead: Everyone else who uses this computer. Each one gets their own space and their own Cielo, and cannot see yours.
settings.people.humanOnly: Only a person can add teammates to this computer.
settings.people.setupsFailed: Could not read the available setups: {reason}
settings.people.tokenNote: This token is shown once. Hand it over — it is how they sign in the first time.
